title: Wrike Review (2026)
intro: Wrike is evaluated here as a work OS / work management platform — Wrike is a work management platform strong with agencies and mid-market/enterprise teams needing proofing, request intake, custom workflows and resource views. Free tier exists; Team ~$10/user/mo annual; Business ~$25; Enterprise/Pinnacle custom. This review uses SoftwareGlimpse’s project-management methodology (ease of use, work planning, automation, collaboration, integrations, reporting, scalability, value, AI), scoring products inside their job cluster rather than against unrelated peers. It is based on first-party research, not hands-on lab testing.
summary: Choose Wrike when agency/enterprise work management with proofing, intake and reporting depth matters.
verdict: Choose Wrike when agency/enterprise work management with proofing, intake and reporting depth matters. Compare Asana/monday for easier cross-functional defaults, ClickUp for value breadth, and Smartsheet for spreadsheet-native PMOs. Scores reflect first-party documentation as of 2026-08-17 — not hands-on product testing. Confirm current packaging, minimums and usage rates on the vendor site before purchase.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Capable but denser than Asana — mid-market/agency admins cope well; SMB may feel heavier.
Strong project/folder structures, Gantt and resource-oriented planning.
Custom workflows and intake forms are a Wrike strength on Business+.
Proofing and cross-team collaboration fit creative/agency work.
Reporting and Work Intelligence analytics are a differentiator — 9.
Team $10 is fine; Business $25 is a steeper jump vs ClickUp/Asana. Affiliate economics excluded.
Work Intelligence AI present; not as consumer-visible as Notion/Motion AI.

pricingSummary: Free; Team $10, Business $25 annual; Enterprise custom. Confirm live.
whoShouldChoose: Choose Wrike when agency/enterprise work management with proofing, intake and reporting depth matters.
whoShouldConsiderAlternatives: Compare Asana/monday for easier cross-functional defaults, ClickUp for value breadth, and Smartsheet for spreadsheet-native PMOs.

faq.question: Is Wrike a project management / work OS tool?
faq.answer: Yes. Wrike is evaluated as a work OS / work management platform for boards, timelines, automations and team collaboration on work. It is not monday sales CRM — that remains a separate CRM product entity where applicable.

faq.question: How is Wrike priced?
faq.answer: Free; Team $10, Business $25 annual; Enterprise custom. Confirm live.

faq.question: Does Wrike have a free plan or free trial?
faq.answer: Yes — a free plan is published. A free trial is documented (about 14 days). Confirm current terms with the vendor.

faq.question: Did SoftwareGlimpse personally test Wrike?
faq.answer: No. This review is based on first-party product and pricing research evidence, not hands-on product usage. Affiliate relationships never influence scores.
